mainTopic: Is there מְעִילָה (misuse of הקדש) with the leftover blood of קרבנות, and the source in the Torah for saying there is none
overview: The גמרא first clarifies the earlier dispute about מעילה in the leftover blood of קרבנות, which flowed out to the נחל קדרון and was sold to gardeners. It says that dispute is only about a rabbinic rule. By Torah law, everyone agrees there is no מעילה in this blood. The גמרא then asks for the Torah source and gives three answers. עולא learns it from the word 'לָכֶם', the blood is 'yours.' דבי רבי שמעון learn it from 'לְכַפֵּר', the blood was given for כפרה and not for מעילה. רבי יוחנן learns it from 'הוּא', so blood before כפרה has the same status as blood after כפרה. The גמרא challenges him: maybe the comparison should go the other way, giving מעילה at both stages. It answers with a general rule: once an item's מצוה is done, there is no מעילה. The עמוד ends by attacking that rule with the case of תרומת הדשן, and the answer comes on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The dispute is only rabbinic; by Torah law there is no מעילה in blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the earlier dispute about מעילה in the leftover blood to the rabbinic level. By Torah law, all agree there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue about rabbinic law. But by Torah law, there is no מעילה with this blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is making a comment on the earlier argument about whether a person who benefits from the leftover blood commits מעילה. It says the argument is only about a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some say there is מעילה in the blood, but even they mean only a rule of חכמים. Everyone agrees that the Torah itself does not apply מעילה to this blood. This explains how the Temple treasurers could sell the blood to gardeners at all.

keyTerms.meaning: One commits מעילה (illegal benefit from הקדש)

steps.whatToRemember: Blood of קרבנות has no מעילה מדאורייתא. Any מעילה in it is only מדרבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one side holds there is Torah-level מעילה in the blood. Both sides agree there is none מדאורייתא. Their argument is only about a rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: They only disagree up to here (i.e., the dispute is limited)
only regarding rabbinic law,
but by Torah law
one does not commit misuse with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion of the dispute about מעילה in the blood by defining how far it reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law there is no מעילה in the blood of קרבנות. The dispute is only rabbinic.

steps.title: What is the source that blood has no מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the Torah teaches that blood has no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule it just stated. This line sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood comes from a holy קרבן, so we might expect it to have מעילה like other הקדש. That is why we need a פסוק to teach that it is different.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source behind the rule in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the blood of קרבנות has no מעילה מדאורייתא?

steps.title: עולא learns it from the word 'לָכֶם'
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns from 'לָכֶם' that the blood belongs to the people, not to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The פסוק says 'to you,' which means it will be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the first source. The word 'לָכֶם' in the פסוק about blood shows that the blood is 'yours,' so there is no מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא יז:יא) says 'I gave it to you on the altar.' 'To you' means the blood is not treated as Temple property. Since מעילה only applies to הקדש, it does not apply to the blood.

phrases.english: Ulla said: The verse states:
"to you": it shall be yours.
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in ויקרא יז:יא: "ואני נתתיו לכם על המזבח".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לָכֶם' teaches that the blood belongs to the people and is not הקדש, so there is no מעילה.

steps.title: דבי רבי שמעון learn it from 'לְכַפֵּר'
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי שמעון learns from 'לְכַפֵּר' that blood was given for כפרה, not for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שמעון taught: 'To make atonement' means I gave it for atonement and not for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second source is given from the same פסוק. The word 'לְכַפֵּר' shows that the blood's only purpose is atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes the blood's role as atonement alone. So the Torah did not attach the laws of מעילה to it. This is a different word in the פסוק from עולא's, but it reaches the same conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי שמעון

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Shimon taught:
"to make atonement": I gave it for atonement,
and not for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel source from a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לְכַפֵּר' teaches that the blood is meant only for כפרה, not for the laws of מעילה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן learns it from 'הוּא': before כפרה is like after כפרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from 'הוּא' that blood has the same status before and after כפרה. Since there is no מעילה after, there is none before either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says 'it is.' Before atonement is like after atonement. Just as after atonement there is no מעילה, so too before atonement there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third source. The word 'הוּא' shows that the blood stays the same, so its status after כפרה also applies before כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the blood has been used for כפרה, its מצוה is done, so it has no מעילה. 'הוּא' ties the two stages together, so the blood has no מעילה even before it is used. This source uses a comparison instead of describing what the blood is for.

keyTerms.meaning: It (is), meaning it stays the same
Before the atonement (before the blood is applied)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
the verse states: "it is",
phrases.notes: The word "הוא" comes from the פסוק "כי הדם הוא בנפש יכפר".

phrases.english: before atonement is like after atonement:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה —
phrases.english: just as after atonement there is no misuse with it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה.
phrases.english: so too before atonement there is no misuse with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא: הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, different source for the same rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הוּא' makes blood before כפרה equal to blood after כפרה. After כפרה there is no מעילה, so there is none before either.

steps.title: Why not compare in the opposite direction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: maybe after כפרה should be like before כפרה, so the blood would have מעילה at both stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that after atonement is like before atonement. Just as before atonement there is מעילה, so too after atonement there is מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's comparison. It points out that 'הוּא' could equally be read the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הוּא' only says the two stages are equal. It does not say which stage sets the rule. If the 'before' stage sets the rule, then the blood would have מעילה even after כפרה, which is the opposite of רבי יוחנן's conclusion.

phrases.english: But say: after atonement is like before atonement:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה —
phrases.english: just as before atonement there is misuse with it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה!
phrases.english: so too after atonement there is misuse with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction of רבי יוחנן's comparison.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison of two stages can go either way. Reversing it gives מעילה at both stages instead of at neither.

steps.title: General rule: once the מצוה is done, there is no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a general rule: nothing whose מצוה has been done is subject to מעילה. So the 'after' stage cannot have מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is nothing whose מצוה has been done that one can still commit מעילה with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. A general rule shows that blood after כפרה definitely has no מעילה, so the comparison can only go in his direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'after' stage is already fixed by a known rule, so it cannot change. That means 'הוּא' must carry the 'after' status back to the 'before' stage, not the reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: There is nothing (introduces a general rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle (נעשית מצותו אין מועלין בו) is a basic rule of the laws of מעילה. It comes up in many places across ש״ס.

phrases.english: There is nothing whose מצוה has been performed
and one still commits misuse with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂית מִצְוָתוֹ וּמוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to a general principle that fixes the 'after' stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison could go either way, giving מעילה at both stages.
steps.terutzMaskana: After כפרה there can be no מעילה because the מצוה is done. So the comparison must go from after to before.

steps.title: Challenge from תרומת הדשן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the general rule: תרומת הדשן has had its מצוה done, yet it still has מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such case? But there is תרומת הדשן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from Step 7 by pointing to a counterexample. The answer comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes taken from the מזבח each morning (תרומת הדשן) have already had their מצוה done, and they must be buried. Yet it is forbidden to benefit from them, and doing so is מעילה. This seems to break the rule that a finished מצוה ends מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it not so? (a sharp challenge)
The removal of ashes from the מזבח each morning

steps.confusionAlert: תרומת הדשן is not the same as the regular removal of ashes to outside the camp (הוצאת הדשן). It is the scoop of ashes placed next to the מזבח, which must stay there and be buried.

phrases.english: And is there not? But there is the removal of the ashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general principle used in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'אין לך דבר שנעשית מצותו ומועלין בו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת הדשן is a clear case where the מצוה is done but מעילה still applies, so the rule seems false.
